sampling_model.design: A known rationally weighted fixed-count randomization law on the explicitly listed support \(\Omega\).
sampling_model.units: A fixed finite population with fixed potential outcomes \(Y_i(0),Y_i(1)\) and fixed treatment-indexed observation indicators \(O_i(0),O_i(1)\).
sampling_model.treatment: The random vector \(A\) is the only stochastic object and has exactly \(m\) treated units.
sampling_model.overlap: Every listed assignment has strictly positive recorded probability; no unit-level marginal-positivity condition is imposed.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There is no sampled nuisance function. Missing sharp-null baseline coordinates range over \(\mathcal C_\delta(a)\) and are eliminated by the finite weak-order maximum.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Under an exchangeable assignment law and an altered deterministic unit-index tie-breaking convention, the supremum Fisher p-value over attrition completions has an extreme-completion closed form.

Imputation-assisted randomization tests that impute once and re-impute under each reassignment have finite-population-exact validity under the article's missingness mechanism, with finite-population-valid confidence regions.
Worst-case Wilcoxon--Mann--Whitney testing with arbitrary missing values has statistic bounds and tie-aware p-value safeguards under the ordinary two-sample reference law.
Lower Fisher p-value functions are super-uniform under any fully specified assignment mechanism and can be inverted with guaranteed coverage.
Exact tied Wilcoxon distributions for a fixed completed sample can be computed by generating-polynomial coefficient extraction.
Exact significance tests under restricted sequential randomization rules can be computed by design-specific recursions.
Effect-increasing rank statistics permit exact inversion for bounded null hypotheses and treatment-effect quantiles.
Conditioning on an ex ante covariate-balance partition gives a randomization test with correct unconditional level.
The saved \(\texttt{cvcrand}\) constrained space supports a clustered permutation test based on residualized cluster-mean contrasts.

body.tldr: Attrition makes both a rank statistic and its randomization reference tail depend on missing sharp-null outcomes. For an explicitly listed rationally weighted fixed-count design, the exact worst-case Wilcoxon-midrank p-value is the maximum over a finite complex of complete weak orders, including equality faces. The envelope is finite-sample valid under arbitrary fixed treatment-indexed observation, computable in \(O((2n+1)^k n|\Omega|\operatorname{poly}(\ell))\) time with a linear one-missing sweep, invertible over additive effects by a finite breakpoint scan, and NP-complete to maximize when \(k\) varies. A saved constrained cluster-randomization support is a concrete conditional-design consumer, provided the endpoint is prespecified and the support is not altered after attrition.

project_justification.gap: Li, Sheng, and Yu obtain a tractable extreme-completion formula under exchangeability and an altered deterministic unit-index tie-breaking convention, while general Fisher theory assumes that the statistic is evaluable. Neither line characterizes the completion optimizer for an arbitrary explicitly weighted support with ordinary midranks and active equality faces.
project_justification.niche: Complete weak orders are the smallest finite object that simultaneously retains assignment-specific rank sums, active equality faces, and rational certificates.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the chamber representation and validity, identifies the fixed-\(k\) and variable-\(k\) computational boundary, performs exact additive-effect inversion, and gives a support-preserving constrained-cluster corollary.

body.related_work: Li, Sheng, and Yu study the same nuisance-supremum move in a complete-randomization regime: exchangeability together with their altered deterministic unit-index tie-breaking convention enables an extreme-completion closed form. That simplification does not carry to ordinary midranks and arbitrary explicitly listed rational weights, for which equality faces can be optimal and the complete weak-order chamber optimizer is required. Heng, Zhang, and Feng develop imputation-assisted randomization tests that impute once and re-impute under each reassignment, prove finite-population-exact validity under their missingness mechanism, and construct finite-population-valid confidence regions. Their re-imputation re-randomization law does not evaluate the supplied rational-support Wilcoxon-midrank completion envelope over \(\mathcal C_\delta(a)\). The regime boundary is therefore compact: complete randomization plus altered index tie-breaking gives the Li--Sheng--Yu closed form; arbitrary explicit rational weights plus ordinary midranks gives the equality-inclusive chamber result here; and the complexity of uniform supports generated by fixed-dimensional balance rules remains unresolved. Zeng, Adams, and Bodenham establish arbitrary-missing Wilcoxon bounds and identify tie-induced failures of statistic-only p-value reasoning under the ordinary two-sample law. Luo, Dasgupta, Xie, and Liu establish finite Fisher validity and inversion for fully specified assignment mechanisms with complete evaluability. Sills provides exact tied-rank computation for a fixed completed sample, while Mehta, Patel, and Wei show that restricted randomization can support specialized exact recursions. Karp supplies the polynomial-reduction framework and \(\textsc{Clique}\) source problem used for the explicit-support lower bound. Hennessy et al. justify ex ante conditional randomization partitions, and Yu et al. document the saved constrained space and the distinct residual-contrast \(\texttt{cptest}\) workflow.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The midrank subset-sum equality characterization and its lowest-tied-block consequence are the load-bearing converse in the \(\textsc{Clique}\) reduction and remain the priority for machine checking. Exact finite enumeration has reproduced the equality-face value \(1\) versus strict-order value \(8/9\), all 210 graph and target instances through four vertices, 1,536 weighted observation schedules, 120 one-missing sweeps, and 145 inversion intervals; these checks are evidence, not proofs.
body.honest_scope: The stated hardness concerns an explicitly listed rationally weighted support. The three regimes remain separate: Li--Sheng--Yu's complete-randomization result uses exchangeability and altered index tie-breaking; the present result treats arbitrary explicit rational weights and ordinary midranks; and no hardness conclusion is claimed for uniform balance-generated supports or fixed-dimensional balance rules. The fixed-\(k\) bound is \(\mathrm{XP}\), and whether an \(\mathrm{FPT}\) algorithm exists remains open. The constrained-cluster result describes a new prespecified-endpoint rank option; it does not validate unchanged \(\texttt{cptest}\), survivor conditioning, respondent-only endpoints, or conditioning on the selected assignment row. As a direct implementation sanity check, \(k=0\) reduces to the ordinary weighted Fisher test; at a singleton support or when the realized-row mass exceeds \(\alpha\), power can be vacuous.
